issues.title: REQ-020.md's AC5 and AC-card live-dispatch cases omit the mandatory 'e_' deep-link prefix in their literal /start dispatch text
issues.description: docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-020.md's AC5 case specifies `/start e0002000-0000-0000-0000-000000000a50__linkedin` and `/start e0002000-0000-0000-0000-000000000a50`, and AC-card specifies `/start e0002000-0000-0000-0000-000000000ac0` -- all three omit the 'e_' prefix apps/bot/src/domain/event.ts's parseStartPayload requires to recognize a deep link at all. Every prior spec dispatching a /start deep link (REQ-016.md, REQ-017.md) always includes the 'e_' prefix. As literally written, AC5's dispatch is silently treated as a payload-less /start, but AC5's own subsequent consent:agree callback_data separately carries the correct 'e_' prefix so the case still happens to reach the right end state; AC-card has no such rescue step, so running it exactly as literally specified routes the user into ordinary profile onboarding ('What's your first name?') instead of ever reaching the event card -- a false FAIL caused entirely by the spec's typo. TEST-RUNNER corrected the harness dispatch text to include the 'e_' prefix for both cases and confirmed both genuinely pass with the real deep-link path exercised.

issues.title: REQ-020.md's AC-card fixture uses an invalid (non-hex) UUID literal for the venue id
issues.description: The AC-card fixture's venue INSERT uses id 'c0002000-0000-0000-0000-00000000ac0v' -- the trailing 'v' is not a valid hex digit, so Postgres rejects the literal with 'invalid input syntax for type uuid'. TEST-RUNNER substituted a valid uuid ('c0002000-0000-0000-0000-00000000ac0a') with no other change and confirmed AC-card passes.
